title: Causeway
description: Hold the islands against the Hollow until the tide rises, in a turn-based tactics crossing.

about: Three wardens hold small islands against the Hollow, who cross the causeway at low tide, until the rising sea drowns them. Every Hollow shows what it will strike before it strikes, so each turn is a puzzle with a visible answer.

Causeway is Sindri's showcase: the place a finished capability proves it can be used in a game somebody would choose to play. Its models, textures, sounds and score are generated in the repository, and it runs on the same scenes, Decay scripts and renderer natively and here in the browser.
proves: Lit low-poly 3D with imported GLB models
controls: Select a warden, a cell or a button

title: Orbital Last Stand
description: Survive waves and boss fights with a growing arsenal.

about: The fleet is gone and someone has to hold the line. Build an unlikely warship while an evacuation corridor closes: survive five sectors over ten minutes, or take a field kit into a twelve-boss gauntlet. Firing is automatic; movement, timing your burst and choosing a build make the difference.

Orbital Last Stand is the forcing function. It recreates a complete game using only the editor and Decay, and every gap it hits is closed as a general Sindri capability rather than something shaped around this game.
proves: 160 modules, 15 enemy types and 12 bosses in Decay
Prefabs and pooled spawning at scale
Weave menus that fit a phone

title: Lamplighter
description: The platformer showcase, becoming a short real game: run, jump and collect coins on the way to the flag.

about: Run and jump across a painted level, pick up the coins and reach the flag. Along the way: a plank ferry, one-way planks, a crate the wind pushes, a lantern on a tether and windmills on powered hinges.

Lamplighter is the platformer genre showcase, becoming a short real game about a courier lighting a valley's lanterns at dusk (see docs/lamplighter-plan.md); today it is still the one painted level. It is where Sindri's plain 2D path is proven: tilemap collision, gravity, collider authoring, camera follow and the 2D Scene view. It is also the project to copy when you start a side-view game of your own.
proves: Coyote time and jump buffering in Decay
Lit caves and sliced UI panels
Sounds made in the Sound Lab

title: Scorchball
description: Local multiplayer football for two to four controllers.

about: Couch football for two to four players, each on their own pad, or one player against a bot. A port of an earlier Unity project, rebuilt as a Sindri project with its original pixel art, sounds and tuning.
Scorchball is the local-multiplayer showcase: gamepads read by player slot, players joining and leaving mid-game, and players made from prefabs were added to Sindri for it.
controls: Play vs Bot or Local Multiplayer
play.note: Best with gamepads. Play vs Bot needs only one.

title: Low Tide
description: Drive your home across a drained sea ahead of the returning Tide.

about: The ocean drained away generations ago and left the Basin. You crew a crawler, a house on treads, and drive it across the old sea floor gathering wood, stone, salt and scrap. Then the Tide returns, and you head uphill before the lowlands flood.

Low Tide is the moving-home showcase: a crew walking a tilemap deck in its own coordinates while the deck drives and turns beneath them, a camera that turns with it, and a top-down game played on the engine's generated voxel terrain. There is no game code: it is a scene and Decay scripts.
proves: A walkable world on a moving, turning parent
Tile reads and writes from Decay
Generated voxel terrain seen as a map
Phone controls that appear on first touch
controls: Take the helm, gather, pick up
W / S · A / D at the helm

title: Flappy
description: A small flapping arcade game.

about: One-button flight through an endless line of gaps. They change height every lap, the course speeds up as the score climbs, and the sky, hills and ground scroll in parallax.
Flappy is the smallest complete game in the repository: one scene and a handful of Decay scripts. Copy it to start a one-button arcade game.
proves: A whole arcade loop in Decay

title: Tween Lab
description: Compare five easing curves with managed Decay playback controls.

about: Five easing curves side by side, applied to movement, scale, colour and rotation. Pause, resume, cancel, restart or replace the running tweens and watch each one answer.
proves: A layout that fits portrait and landscape
controls: Shortcuts are shown on each button

title: Camera Lab
description: Explore camera follow, dead zones, smoothing, confinement and impact shake.

about: Follow, dead zones, smoothing, confinement and impact shake, with visible guides so you can see what the camera is doing and why. Start the tour to take the target beyond the camera's limits.
controls: Follow, bounds, shake, smoothing, dead zone

title: Spatial Query Lab
description: Explore nearest targets and ordered radius results with tags, active state and parent transforms.

about: Move a query origin and watch the nearest tagged entity and every target inside the radius, listed in order. Change tags, disable targets or rotate a parent to see that the queries compare real world positions.
controls: Toggle a target, its parent, rotate the parent

title: Physics Playground
description: A room full of contraptions, from a wrecking ball to a crane, with tools to grab, blast, spawn and probe them.

about: One room full of contraptions and the tools to poke them: a wrecking ball, a gantry crane, a cannon gallery, a bumper pit, a material lab, a seesaw, a robot on a test track, a domino run and a voxel quarry in 3D. Grab, blast, spawn and probe anything.
proves: 3D bodies on a diggable voxel floor

title: Input Actions
description: Steer by what you mean, not what you press, and rebind boost to any key or button while it runs.

about: The ship reads what the player means rather than what they pressed. Steer with WASD, the arrows or a d-pad, boost with Space or a pad, and rebind boost to any key or button while it runs.
proves: Arena sized from the Weave layout

title: Sound Mixer
description: Turn the master, music and effects buses up and down while the theme plays.

about: Every sound plays through a bus, and every bus through master. Drag a slider and hear the theme and effects change as they play. Browsers start audio on the first click or key.

title: Sequence Stage
description: A ship flies in on a sequence authored in the Timeline, with sound cues, then the stage idles on a loop. Space or tap replays it.

about: A ship flies in on a sequence authored in the editor's Timeline, with sound cues, then the stage idles on a loop. The script only says which sequence plays; every track is authored data.
proves: One director driving the whole scene

title: Sprite Shaders
description: Four project WGSL sprite shaders side by side: a pulsing outline, a dissolve, a hit flash and a wave. Scripts drive the burn and the flash through each sprite's shader parameters; Space flashes.

about: Five copies of one badge: no shader, then a pulsing outline, a dissolve, a hit flash and a wave. Each shader is one WGSL function the engine wraps in its sprite pipeline, and scripts drive their parameters.

title: Sprite Masks
description: A keyhole wanders over a night sky: the night is masked outside it so a sunny meadow shows through, and a gem masked inside it is only ever seen through the hole.

about: A keyhole wanders over a night sky. The night is masked outside it, so a sunny meadow shows through, and a gem masked inside it is only ever seen through the hole.
proves: Masks that move with a script

title: Weave Control Room
description: Toggle, type and scroll through engine widgets styled by Weave.

about: Engine widgets styled by Weave and driven by Decay: switches, a checkbox, a locked control, a Unicode callsign field with a caret and selection, and a clipped archive that scrolls by wheel, drag or keyboard focus.
proves: Focus navigation by keyboard and pad
Text input, including on a phone

title: Weave UI
description: Explore CSS-inspired responsive UI, layouts and presentation rules.

about: One scene recomposed for desktop and portrait viewports through presentation rules that resolve into ordinary Sindri UI data. Resize the window, or turn your phone, to see it change.

title: Voxel Lab
description: Inspect voxel terrain, meshing and rendering effects.

about: Sindri's voxel world on its own: generated terrain streamed in sections, meshed and lit, with the renderer's effects exposed so they can be inspected one at a time.

title: Particle Lab
description: Design and preview Sindri particle emitters.

about: Tune a Sindri particle emitter and copy or download its component JSON. The editor can apply it to a selected emitter.

title: Sound Lab
description: Make game sound effects and chiptune music in the browser, then download them.

about: Make a game's coin, jump, laser and explosion sounds, or a chiptune song, then download them. From the desktop, the same tool sends them straight into a Sindri project; the platformer's sounds were made with it.

title: Sprite Baker
description: Drop in a Blender model (.glb, .gltf, .obj or a .zip of one) or write a recipe, and bake it into ordinary Sindri sprites in the browser, in isometric, top-down or side view.

about: Drop in a model made in Blender (a .glb, .gltf or .obj, or the .zip or folder it came in) and it is centred on a tile, shaded into the same four-shade palette as everything else, and baked in four directions, each drawn on the floor it will stand on. Fit it, turn it, recolor its materials and tune the light with the inspector, or write a recipe of boxes, cylinders and spheres by hand. Download the PNG, its .sheet and the prefab, or all three as a zip laid out like a project's assets. The same pipeline runs offline from the command line for recipes made of primitives.

title: Shapes Lab
description: Procedural shapes and geometry in motion.

about: Sindri's zero-art proving ground: a reactor, a boss, a ship and orbitals built only from engine shapes, hierarchy, transforms, blending and Decay. Not a single texture.

title: 3D Transform Lab
description: A cube faces a raised goal and walks to it in world space while the camera orbits the scene.

about: A cube faces a raised goal and walks to it in world space while a perspective camera orbits the scene. It starts under a scaled parent, and its script uses world coordinates so the parent does not change its speed.

title: 3D Orbit Camera Lab
description: A third-person orbit camera follows a walker, pulls in past a barrier and eases back out. Right-drag, or click to capture the pointer, to look around.

about: A third-person orbit camera follows a walker to a raised goal. A barrier blocks the camera's requested distance, so it pulls in, keeps facing the walker, then eases back out when the barrier is removed.

title: 3D Character Lab
description: Ride a ferry, jump off and walk to the goal pad with grounded 3D character movement. WASD moves, Space jumps.

about: Ride a gold ferry, jump off and walk to the goal pad. Gravity, jumping and speed are Decay gameplay; the engine clips movement, classifies support and carries the character on the moving platform.

title: Model Collision Lab
description: Walk around a wall that collides from an imported GLB's own triangles. WASD moves.

about: Walk around a wall that collides from an imported GLB's own triangles. One model holds both the ground and the wall, and the same asset is drawn and collided with.

title: 3D Lighting Lab
description: Point and spot lights, the sun, ambient fill and the sky change color and direction from Decay.

about: Point and spot lights, the sun, ambient fill and the sky change colour and direction from Decay. Two panels compare single- and double-sided materials.

title: Day/Night Lab
description: A twelve-second day moves through sunrise, midday, sunset and night, then mounted lights take over.

about: A twelve-second day moves through sunrise, midday, sunset and night. The sun turns and the sky shifts, then the work lights mounted on a moving prop take over.
